title: Programme Office Ruling on the Holdback While a Traded Piece May Still Be Taken Back
content:
Ruling of the programme office on the Belrose Trade-In and Upgrade Programmes: while the window in which the traded piece may still be taken back is open, an amount is held back from the credit put toward a sale, and the amount depends on whether the piece has been inspected.

## The ruling

Where the credit was issued within the window in which the traded piece may still be taken back and the registration's entries carry a condition inspection of the piece, five hundred (500 USD) is held back. Where the credit was issued within that window and those entries carry no condition inspection, fifteen hundred (1500 USD) is held back. Where the credit was issued outside that window, nothing is held back.

The days since the credit was issued are counted in calendar days from the issue date on the registration to the handling date, and the credit was issued within the window while that count does not exceed the programme's published window for taking the piece back. A condition inspection stands among the entries where an inspection entry is recorded against the registration.

## The window by programme

| Programme | Window in which the piece may be taken back (calendar days) |
|---|---|
| Belrose Standard Trade-In | 7 |
| Diamond Trade-Up Guarantee | 14 |
| Bridal Upgrade Guarantee | 14 |
| Lifetime Diamond Upgrade Guarantee | 21 |
| Signature Collection Upgrade Privilege | 30 |
| Estate Purchase and Consignment Programme | 10 |

## Cases under a programme whose window is 14 calendar days

| Days since the credit was issued | Inspection among the entries | Held back (USD) |
|---|---|---|
| 10 | yes | 500 |
| 10 | no | 1500 |
| 14 | yes | 500 |
| 15 | yes | 0 |
| 15 | no | 0 |

A credit issued exactly 14 days ago is within that window; one issued 15 days ago is outside it.
